items.title: Defining Industry 4.0 and the Fourth Industrial Revolution
items.abstract: Industry 4.0 is frequently described through its technologies: cyber-physical systems, the Internet of Things, artificial intelligence, advanced analytics, cloud and edge computing, robotics, digital twins and platform infrastructures. Such descriptions are useful, but incomplete. They explain what has become technically possible but do not adequately explain why the organisational and human consequences are so substantial. This chapter therefore defines Industry 4.0 and the wider Fourth Industrial Revolution through a socio-technical systems perspective. It distinguishes the industrial concept of Industry 4.0 from the broader societal idea of the Fourth Industrial Revolution, examines the convergence and interdependence that differentiate the present transition from earlier waves of digitisation, and considers the implications for work, knowledge, authority, identity and institutional arrangements. The central argument is that Industry 4.0 is best understood as a reconfiguration of relationships among people, technologies, organisations and institutions. Its significance lies not in the presence of intelligent technologies alone, but in the redistribution of sensing, interpretation and decision-making across human and machine actors. Human transformation is consequently not an adjunct to technological adoption. It is a constitutive element of the transformation itself.

items.title: Deriving Metacognitive Scaffolding Design Principles and an Integrated Model for Generative AI–Supported Major Exploration
items.abstract: As flexible major selection systems, including undeclared admission, become increasingly widespread in higher education, learners' capacity for self-directed academic and career planning has become more important than ever.Although the widespread adoption of Generative AI (GenAI) has improved the efficiency of information acquisition, it also raises concerns about intensified cognitive offloading, whereby learners become overly dependent on AI-generated responses without engaging in critical thinking.To address this issue, this study proposes an AI-based integrated metacognitive scaffolding model that enables learners to use AI not merely as an information provider, but as a tool for expanding their thinking.To this end, an integrative literature review explored the theoretical relationship between metacognition and scaffolding, and a cross-mapping analysis was used to derive stage-specific design principles.In addition, a scenario-based walkthrough examined the logical applicability of the proposed model.The analysis suggests that AI-supported major exploration can be conceptually organized around the role of an Inquiring Coach.The proposed model organizes the learning process into three metacognitive phases-Planning, Monitoring, and Evaluation-and specifies stage-specific strategies, including delaying immediate answers, detecting inconsistencies and generating counter-questions, and promoting reflective self-explanation.The model also incorporates a Fading mechanism as a design principle intended to support the gradual development of learners' selfdirected exploration.This study provides conceptual design guidelines for AI-supported career education systems.It proposes a theoretical basis for shifting attention from information-delivery efficiency to designing interactions that support learners' thinking.However, the model's effects on learners' metacognition or career decision-making were not empirically tested.

items.title: Design and analysis of an affordable manual sit-to-stand wheelchair for disabled individuals
items.abstract: PURPOSE: The individuals with lower-limb disabilities often experience considerable difficulty during sit-to-stand (STS) transitions, limiting their independence and increasing reliance on caregivers. According to the World Health Organisation (WHO, 2023), nearly 80 million people worldwide require wheelchairs. METHOD: This study presents the design and performance evaluation of an affordable manual sit-to-stand wheelchair that incorporates ergonomic and anthropometric design principles with a three-bar linkage mechanism, ball screw drive, scissor-lift structure, force-balancing mechanism, and optimised gear ratio to ensure stable, controlled, and energy-efficient operation without electrical actuators. Structural validation of design using finite element analysis demonstrated a maximum frame deformation of 2.2 mm and a factor of safety of 2.5 under a static load of 120 kg, confirming the mechanical reliability of the design. Human testing is conducted with 25 participants (15 wheelchair users and 10 healthy volunteers), while clinical evaluation is performed under a physiotherapist's supervision using standardised functional assessment protocols. RESULT: The average sit-to-stand transition time is 9.5 ± 1.8 s, with 90% of participants achieving successful independent standing. Force analysis indicated that the proposed linkage mechanism reduced the operating force to approximately 10 N, corresponding to a 45.6% reduction in user effort. Furthermore, usability assessment yielded a mean System Usability Scale (SUS) score of 86.3/100, indicating excellent user acceptance. CONCLUSION: The findings demonstrate that the proposed STS wheelchair is a safe, mechanically robust, and cost-effective assistive mobility solution that enhances user independence, reduces caregiver burden, and improves the quality of life for individuals with mobility impairments, particularly in low-resource settings.

items.title: Design and Field Validation of a VR-Based RAG Historical NPC: Knowledge Grounding and Persona Grounding Can Fail Independently
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based non-player characters (NPCs) can support unscripted historical dialogue, but their behavior in deployed educational virtual reality (VR) settings remains underexamined. This study reports the design and field validation of a self-hosted VR platform in which a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) NPC, representing King Sejong the Great, engaged 42 international participants across 126 intercultural-learning sessions. The analytic corpus, reconstructed from retained session logs, comprised 104 sessions from 39 participants (2053 participant turns; 2053 NPC responses). Repetitive NPC response loops occurred in 33 sessions (31.7%), spanning 54 episodes and 190 responses, and co-occurred with learner-side transcript repetition in 31 of these sessions. The NPC maintained its first-person persona throughout the screened corpus, yet produced 30 biographical claims unsupported by the historical record: persona consistency did not ensure factual grounding. Prompt compliance varied by instruction type, and a post hoc implementation audit could not confirm that retrieved content contributed to individual responses. Together, these results identify persona grounding, knowledge grounding, retrieval observability, and session-level instrumentation as validation targets that deployed VR–LLM systems must address separately.

items.title: DESIGN METHODS FOR RESPONSIVE COMMERCIAL WEBSITE INTERFACES BASED ON MOBILE INTERACTION PATTERNS
items.abstract: In the current digital landscape, the success of mobile commerce is tied directly to the quality of the user interface. This study examines how shifting to a "Mobile First" philosophy fundamentally reshapes the architecture of web applications. We look beyond mere technical specifications to explore the physics of user-screen interaction—from the ergonomics of "active finger" movements to reducing page weight by stripping away bulky third-party frameworks. Our research demonstrates that leveraging native HTML5/CSS3 code alongside flexible layouts (Grid and Flexbox) creates interfaces that are not only lightning-fast but also intuitively adaptive to human behavior.

items.title: Designing assessment for GenAI contexts
items.abstract: This chapter argues that defensive responses to generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) and academic integrity, while understandable, focus on the wrong problem. Rather than asking how to contain or neutralise GenAI, we might ask how its emergence exposes long-standing weaknesses in assessment design and opens opportunities for transformation. Learning has always been collective and distributed across people, technologies, and contexts, yet dominant systems continue to treat knowledge as the property of isolated learners. Drawing on an entangled pedagogy perspective, the chapter challenges the individualistic assumptions underpinning traditional assessment. GenAI makes the fiction of autonomous academic work visible, exposing the fragility of product-based, grade-focused assessment. Reconceptualising academic integrity as collective, relational, and situated rather than individual and rule-based, this chapter argues for framing it not by what students must avoid but by what they must learn to do: engage ethically and purposefully with resources, including AI, while navigating complex learning contexts. Assessment is reimagined as codesigned and collaborative, with students actively shaping criteria, parameters, and outcomes. In this vision, assessment cultivates the adaptive capacity required for professional and social life, where competence emerges through collectively orchestrating human and technological resources in ways that reflect the entangled nature of learning in a complex world.

items.title: Designing Backup-Supporting Information Displays for Multi-Human Multi-Agent Teams in Drone Swarm Supervision
items.abstract: Search-and-rescue (SAR) drone swarms increasingly require multi-operator supervision, in which backup behaviors redistribute cognitive load to improve performance but introduce trade-offs in situational awareness (SA) and task engagement. Existing human-autonomy teaming interfaces present symmetric displays across all roles, ignoring the asymmetric information needs of backup providers and recipients. We developed a two-human, eight-drone Unity SAR testbed that operationalizes three team structures (independent, Operator A-busy, Operator B-busy) via event-allocation manipulation, with a SPAM (Situation Present Assessment Method)-derived in-task SA probe. Three iterative focus groups with eight human-centered design researchers and professionals yielded four display conditions: no-display baseline, effort display, urgency display, and combined. Semi-structured interviews with three SAR practitioners confirmed high realism ratings for the overall testbed and the viability of dynamic backup. A feasibility pilot study ( N = 4) revealed a significant main effect of team structure on backup count, confirming that the manipulation elicits backup behaviors as designed.

items.title: Designing for Social Presence in AR/MR: Dimensions, Patterns, and Research Directions
items.abstract: The rise of virtual reality (VR), mixed reality (MR), and augmented reality (AR) head-mounted displays (HMDs) has expanded the design space for social extended reality (XR) systems. However, creating realistic social XR experiences with high social presence remains challenging. Based on a screening of 3,414 studies and thematic analysis of 250 papers published between 2015 and 2021, followed by a validation of the resulting design space through the categorization of 258 studies published between 2022 and 2026, we identify (1) seven common social interaction patterns in AR/MR, (2) thirteen design dimensions for supporting all levels of social presence while developing social AR/MR solutions, (3) future research opportunities, and (4) a practitioner guide that translates the extracted design dimensions into actionable design considerations. Through our work, researchers, developers, and designers can develop realistic, engaging social AR/MR solutions that foster social connection and bring minds closer together.

items.title: Developing Consumer Trust in Sustainable Agentic Commerce: Conditional Signals, Auditable Governance, and Justified Non-Purchase Advice
items.abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) changes digital retail from consumer-led search to delegated decision making, increasing both the potential value and the agency risks of recommendation. This conceptual article asks the following: Under what architectural and governance conditions can an autonomous shopping agent earn calibrated consumer trust while supporting economically and environmentally appropriate consumption decisions? Using a purposive, multidisciplinary synthesis of signaling theory, principal–agent theory, the ability–benevolence–integrity model of trust, trustworthy AI, recommender system governance, and sustainable consumption research, we develop a process model linking four architectural features to consumer perceptions, delegation, reliance, and decision outcomes. The features are scoped provenance verification, disclosed and audited commercial incentives, faithful contrastive explanations, and active evaluation of retention, repair, refurbishment, and purchase. We argue that justified non-purchase advice can function as a credible signal of consumer alignment only when the operator is the signal sender, the advice creates observable opportunity or accountability costs, and compensation and audit arrangements make imitation more costly for a misaligned operator. The framework distinguishes perceived trustworthiness from overall trust, willingness to delegate, actual reliance, recommendation appropriateness, and lifecycle sustainability. A five-layer architecture, a worked decision example, and four testable propositions specify how missing data, conflicting preferences, uncertainty, authorization, privacy, and accountability should be handled. This article treats the applications as illustrations rather than empirical cases and concludes with limitations and an empirical research agenda focused on calibrated—not merely increased—trust.

items.title: Developing student voice through oral assessment
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is not new. The limitation of assessment regimes in higher education is not new. Advances in AI have raised sector-wide, urgent concerns about assessment’s limitations. Amongst all the hype, reactions, and responses—including regulators in some countries, like Australia, calling for action on assessment—I revisit the purpose of assessment evoked by David Boud, the practices of oral assessment as theorised by Gordon Joughin, and the authority of finding your student voice as conceptualised by Alison Cook-Sather. I argue that sustainable assessment in the age of AI requires oral assessment to be enacted as a learner–teacher dialogic practice infused with a student voice ethos. Rather than treating oral assessment as a technical response to AI, I position it as a relational and pedagogical practice that supports learning now while preparing students for futures in which AI will be ever-present. I situate my argument in conversation with those scholars calling for rehumanising, inclusive and socially just assessment practices.

items.title: Development and evaluation of a human-centered adaptive workstation for large planar workpieces: prospects for end-of-life vehicle disassembly
items.abstract: Abstract Performing manual tasks involves ergonomic risk factors associated with musculoskeletal disorders. This paper presents an adaptive workstation designed to adjust the working height according to individual anthropometric characteristics and evaluates its effects on posture, perceived strain, and the duration of value-adding activities. The study examined abstracted manual tasks with relevance to end-of-life vehicle disassembly. A proof-of-concept study with twelve participants shows that more frequent height adjustments reduce exposure to ergonomically unfavorable joint-angle ranges and perceived strain without significantly affecting the duration of value-adding activities. Adaptive systems therefore have the potential to reduce awkward postures in end-of-life vehicle disassembly. The findings should be examined in a dedicated disassembly use case, taking into account varying product conditions and appropriate positioning of the work object for tasks requiring high force exertion. Practical Relevance : This paper presents an adaptive workstation that can be adjusted for various (dis-)assembly and maintenance applications. The findings of the proof-of-concept study suggest that adaptive systems offer prospects for reducing physical stress and strain during manual tasks.

items.title: Development and validation of an artificial intelligence model for automated classification of whole-body bone scintigraphy in oncology patients
items.abstract: Whole-body bone scintigraphy with Tc-99 m methylene diphosphonate (MDP) is widely used to detect osseous metastases, and artificial intelligence (AI) may support its interpretation. We developed and internally validated OsseoScan AI, a deep learning model classifying whole-body bone scans as normal or abnormal. In this retrospective single-center study at Phrapokklao Hospital, Thailand, consecutive oncologic scans from April 2021 to June 2026 were labeled using a two-tier composite reference standard. An ImageNet-21k-pretrained EfficientNetV2-B3 was trained on full-body anterior and posterior images from 5,040 scans of 4,313 patients (1,395 abnormal), partitioned at patient level into a training/validation pool (4,032 scans; 5-fold cross-validation) and a held-out test set (1,008 scans). Pooled out-of-fold AUC was 0.959 (95% CI 0.952–0.967). On the test set at the pre-specified threshold, AUC was 0.963 (0.946–0.977), sensitivity was 0.907 (0.868–0.944), specificity was 0.886 (0.862–0.910), and NPV was 0.961. Sensitivity was 1.000 for extensive, 0.925 for multifocal, and 0.725 for solitary metastases; a sensitivity-oriented threshold raised solitary-lesion sensitivity to 0.882 while flagging 40.7% of scans. Grad-CAM provided qualitative explainability. OsseoScan AI showed high discrimination in internal validation and may support worklist prioritization; external, multi-center, and prospective evaluation is required before clinical use.

items.title: Development and Validation of an Artificial Intelligence-Supported Educational Brochure for the Prevention of Drug Use and HIV Infection
items.abstract: Introduction: Drug use and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection remain major public health challenges, particularly among adolescents and young adults. Educational materials supported by artificial intelligence (AI) represent an innovative approach to health promotion strategies. Objective: To develop and validate an artificial intelligence-supported educational brochure for the prevention of drug use and HIV infection among adolescents and young adults. Methods: A technological development study with a mixed-methods approach was conducted at the Universidad de Ciencias Médicas de Santiago de Cuba between August and October 2026. The development of the brochure comprised three phases: literature review and scientific content curation, AI-assisted graphic design, and expert validation. Means, standard deviations, and the Content Validity Index (CVI) were calculated. Results: An educational brochure was developed in both printed and digital formats addressing the prevention of drug use and HIV infection. The overall CVI was 0.96, and mean scores ranged from 4.63 to 4.88. Overall, 93.8% of responses were rated as "Agree" or "Strongly Agree." Conclusions: The educational brochure demonstrated adequate content validity and represents a useful educational resource for strengthening the prevention of drug use and HIV infection. Artificial intelligence proved to be an effective supportive tool when its use was accompanied by expert supervision and validation.

items.title: Diabetes Prediction in Adults Through AI Techniques Within the Metaverse Framework
items.abstract: Diabetes mellitus is a most common and chronic disease, affecting millions of people worldwide that presents substantial morbidity, mortality, and economic costs to society. This chapter helps to incorporate artificial intelligence (AI) along with metaverse for adult diabetes prediction. In this chapter, we provide an extensive review of current research and literature on AI-based diabetes prediction, concentrating specifically in machine learning (ML) methods and deep learning (DL) techniques. This report examines a wide range of datasets and preprocessing methods to help you select the right data, cleaning approaches for that data, and the algorithms best suited. Best practices in each are 200 identified and explored throughout. More studies are needed to enhance the interpretability and robustness of models for widespread clinical application. Future exploration is suggested in the creation of transparent AI inside metaverse, with particular ways to deal with personalized medicine and ethical use of patient data. Collaboration between health-care professionals, AI researchers, and virtual environment developers will be needed to take this field further forward in the realization of the full potential that metaverse has for us.

items.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Artificial Intelligence for Detecting ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction on 12-Lead Electrocardiograms
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) may improve electrocardiographic detection of ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), but available studies address distinct diagnostic questions. We systematically reviewed studies evaluating AI-based STEMI detection from 12-lead electrocardiograms and separately synthesized AI performance against a clinical reference standard, AI and clinician performance against a clinical reference, and AI agreement with physician electrocardiogram (ECG) interpretation. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, Cochrane Library, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from January 2010 through March 10, 2025. Bivariate random-effects models generated pooled sensitivity, specificity, and hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (AUC). Twenty-six studies comprising 539,876 ECGs were included. In 20 studies comparing AI with a clinical reference standard, pooled sensitivity was 0.95 (95% confidence interval, 0.91-0.97), specificity 0.95 (0.90-0.98), AUC 0.98 (0.97-0.99), positive likelihood ratio 19.2 (9.3-39.5), and negative likelihood ratio 0.05 (0.03-0.10). In 8 studies reporting both AI and clinician performance against a clinical reference, separate syntheses showed sensitivity of 0.91 (0.86-0.94) for AI versus 0.78 (0.69-0.85) for clinicians, specificity of 0.91 (0.82-0.96) for both, and AUCs of 0.95 and 0.90, respectively. In 7 studies using physician ECG interpretation as the comparator, AI sensitivity was 0.85 (0.70-0.94), specificity 0.99 (0.96-1.00), and AUC 0.98 (0.96-0.99). Sensitivity analyses excluding case-control designs, influential studies, and restricting analyses to deep learning models or raw waveform ECGs produced similar findings.

items.title: Diagnostic Validity, External Validation, and Clinical Utility of Multimodal Artificial Intelligence for Depression and Anxiety Detection in Adults: A Critical Review
items.abstract: Multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) combines behavioural, linguistic, physiological, questionnaire and contextual signals to identify depression or anxiety. Although reported discrimination is frequently promising, diagnostic accuracy, transportability and clinical benefit represent different evidential questions. This critical narrative review examines adult-focused multimodal systems, the validity of their reference standards, the strength of internal and external evaluation, and the evidence required before clinical deployment. Literature published from January 2014 to 23 August 2026 was examined alongside earlier methodological and measurement studies. Sources were selected for relevance to diagnostic constructs, study design, model assessment, external validation and clinical implementation. The synthesis distinguishes clinician-assessed disorders from questionnaire thresholds, symptom trajectories, induced anxiety states and benchmark-derived labels. Recent multimodal depression studies include a geographically independent validation with strong case–control discrimination, whereas a naturalistic speech study using structured diagnostic interviews showed substantially more modest performance and little incremental benefit beyond conventional rating scales. Syntheses of model performance remain vulnerable to heterogeneous reference standards, retrospective study designs, selective cohorts and dependence on repeatedly reused datasets. Evidence for anxiety is particularly fragmented: physiological and smartphone models often predict momentary arousal or elevated questionnaire scores rather than independently diagnosed anxiety disorders. Apparent gains from fusion must therefore be evaluated against simple clinical comparators, missing-modality patterns, calibration, subgroup reliability, data burden and downstream consequences. A staged translational framework is proposed, separating analytical validity, diagnostic validity, external reproducibility and patient-centred utility. Priority studies should prospectively recruit consecutive or representative clinical populations, employ blinded structured assessments, prespecify thresholds, report calibration and decision consequences, and compare multimodal models with feasible care pathways. Multimodal AI has credible research value as an adjunct to assessment and symptom monitoring; evidence for autonomous diagnosis or improved adult clinical outcomes remains insufficient.

items.title: Digital Cash-to-Cash Transformation and Organizational Resilience: Evidence from Working-Capital Buffer Configuration
items.abstract: Abstract Digital transformation is increasingly important for firms seeking to remain resilient under conditions of uncertainty, yet less is known about how digital technologies strengthen resilience when they are embedded in specific operating routines. This study examines whether digital cash-to-cash transformation, the digital redesign and operational integration of inventory, receivables, and payables routines, enhances organisational resilience. Using Chinese listed firms from 2012 to 2024, we construct a large-language-model-based textual measure from annual reports that distinguishes substantive digital transformation in working-capital processes from generic digital disclosure. The results show that digital cash-to-cash transformation is positively associated with a multidimensional measure of organisational resilience. This finding remains robust to alternative measures, instrumental-variable estimation, propensity score matching, double machine learning, and shock-based tests. Mechanism analyses indicate that the resilience benefits of digital transformation arise primarily through working-capital buffer configuration rather than simple cash-cycle compression. Specifically, digital transformation is associated with higher inventory, receivables, and payables postures, each of which is positively related to resilience. The effects are stronger among more focused firms and firms pursuing differentiation strategies. These findings suggest that the resilience value of digital transformation lies not merely in adopting digital technologies, but in embedding them in cash-to-cash routines that improve information visibility, coordination, and the flexible deployment of working-capital resources.

items.title: Digital Competency and Student Engagement: A Literature Review on Deep Learning Integration in Primary Education
items.abstract: This research presents a literature review that investigates how digital competencies relate to student engagement, particularly in the integration of deep learning in primary education. Drawing on findings from a diverse range of peer-reviewed studies published between 2018 and 2025, this review highlights that digital proficiency, including digital literacy, skills, and creativity, is closely associated with students’ cognitive, emotional, and behavioral engagement. The effective use of digital resources, such as artificial intelligence, virtual reality, and adaptive learning systems, promotes critical thinking and facilitates deep learning. The findings show that students with advanced digital capabilities demonstrate greater concentration and enthusiasm, whereas those with limited skills and autonomy are more likely to disengage and exhibit off-task behaviors online. Additional factors, such as personalized learning, social and emotional engagement, and teacher’s digital expertise also influence this relationship. Identified challenges include digital disparities, insufficient teacher preparation, and distractions from non-educational digital activities. To address these challenges, targeted digital literacy initiatives and improvements in curriculum design are recommended. In summary, this review highlights the complex relationship between digital competencies and student engagement, emphasizing the importance of comprehensive curriculum integration and teacher support to enhance learning outcomes through deep learning approaches in primary education.

items.title: Digital Imperialism in Skilled Migration Platforms and the Marxist Political Economy of Extraction
items.abstract: Digital diaspora represents a modality of digital imperialism in which platform governance, IP and data capture, and a transnational reserve army of skilled labor jointly organize cross-border surplus extraction and reproduce global uneven development. The key mechanisms include sponsorship and platform rents that enable wage arbitrage under algorithmic management, concentration of value through ownership of code, patents, data, and behavioral traces institutionalized via End User License Agreements (EULAs) and Terms of Service (ToS), and the persistent oversupply of credentialed workers produced by higher-education expansion and student-to-work visa pipelines. Empirically, the article draws on the U.S. H-1B pipeline and Nairobi content-moderator litigation to illustrate how sponsorship dependency, algorithmic quotas, and extraterritorial platform governance discipline skilled labor. Holding occupation and tenure constant, greater algorithmic opacity and sponsorship dependency tend to produce wider North–South wage differentials and greater concentration of IP and data value in core jurisdictions, while restrictive EULAs further limit workers’ ability to transfer reputational capital across platforms. This article argues that digital diaspora functions as a modality of digital imperialism through three mechanisms: (1) sponsorship-based wage arbitrage, (2) IP and data capture, and (3) algorithmic control over skilled labor. Its contribution lies in unifying digital-labor and high-skilled migration studies, specifying IP/data capture as a primary circuit of extraction, and theorizing the reserve army of skilled labor as central to digital imperialism.

items.title: Digital Investigation Techniques, Artificial Intelligence, and Mechanisms for Documenting International Humanitarian Law Violations
items.abstract: The documentation of violations of international humanitarian law has been transformed by the digital age. Where accountability once depended almost entirely on the testimony of witnesses and the recovery of physical evidence, investigators now draw on a vast and growing body of digital material, photographs, videos, satellite imagery and social-media posts, and on artificial-intelligence tools capable of processing it at a scale no human team could match. This article examines digital investigation techniques, artificial intelligence, and the mechanisms for documenting violations of international humanitarian law. It sets out the concepts of the violation and the documentation imperative, the principal techniques of digital open-source investigation, and the role and risks of artificial intelligence; it examines the legal and normative framework, comprising the Geneva Conventions and their Additional Protocols, the Rome Statute, the Berkeley Protocol on Digital Open Source Investigations, and the Ugandan framework under the International Criminal Court Act Cap 14, the Evidence Act Cap 8, the Electronic Transactions Act Cap 99 and the Computer Misuse Act Cap 96; and it analyses the reception of digital evidence before international courts through cases including Prosecutor v Al-Werfalli, Prosecutor v Al Hassan, Prosecutor v Tadic, Prosecutor v Lubanga and Prosecutor v Ongwen, and the work of mechanisms such as the IIIM for Syria, UNITAD and the eyeWitness project. The article argues that digital and artificial-intelligence techniques offer a powerful means of preserving evidence and overcoming the obstacles to accountability, but that their promise depends on rigorous standards of authentication, verification, transparency and the protection of privacy and witnesses, and it recommends the adoption of the Berkeley Protocol, governance of artificial intelligence, and the modernisation of national rules on electronic evidence.

items.title: DIGITAL STRATEGIC MANAGEMENT OF AN ENTERPRISE: DATA ANALYSIS METHODS, CONTENT MANAGEMENT AND PR, LEADERSHIP, TEAM INTERACTION, AND INTERCULTURAL COMMUNICATION
items.abstract: The article substantiates the conceptual foundations of digital strategic management of an enterprise as an integrated management system based on digital technologies, data analytics, communication platforms, and modern organizational approaches. The relevance of the study is determined by the acceleration of digital transformation, increasing information volumes, intensification of competition, and growing uncertainty of the business environment. The key components of digital strategic management are identified and systematized, including data analysis methods, content management and PR, digital leadership, team interaction, and intercultural communication. The functional role of each component is determined. Data analysis methods, including statistical, comparative, correlation, regression, factor, and cluster analysis, combined with Business Intelligence, Big Data, Predictive Analytics, artificial intelligence, and machine learning, provide an analytical and predictive basis for strategic decision-making, risk identification, and forecasting. Content management and digital PR support stakeholder interaction, corporate reputation, information openness, and communication of strategic objectives and organizational values. Digital leadership is considered a mechanism for coordinating digital transformation, managing change, and developing digital organizational culture. Team interaction ensures the implementation of managerial decisions through digital platforms, cloud services, project management systems, and collaborative communication tools. Intercultural communication contributes to effective international interaction, reduction of communication barriers, and development of business partnerships. The scientific contribution of the study consists in integrating these components into a unified architecture of digital strategic management based on the functional sequence of data and analytics, strategic decision-making, digital leadership, team implementation, communication interaction, and strategic results. The proposed approach provides a basis for enhancing enterprise adaptability, strategic flexibility, competitiveness, and resilience under conditions of digital transformation and environmental uncertainty.

items.title: Digital Technologies and the Re/bordering Practices of Empire: How Digital Coyotes and Charge-for-Charge Businesses Transform the Trails for Precarious Migrants
items.abstract: In the United States, both Republican and Democratic administrations have expanded militarized border infrastructures. While Trump prioritized physical wall construction, Biden redirected investment toward surveillance technologies, advancing a “virtual wall.” Across administrations, binational agreements have fostered new forms of digital border power. Drawing on community-engaged ethnographic fieldwork with Latin American migrants traveling through Mexico, this article examines how digital technologies mediate contemporary re/bordering practices and reshape migrant mobility. I develop a framework for analyzing how evolving sociotechnical assemblages produce new forms of control. Technologies such as the CBP One™ app and migrants’ mobile devices generate digital, spatial, and economic bordering practices that enable exploitation by state and nonstate actors, including digital coyotes and charge-for-charge businesses. At the same time, pro-migrant solidarity networks create provisional shelter, which I conceptualize as transient refuge. Attending to migrants’ perceptions of safety and movement, the study demonstrates how digital technologies reconfigure the spatial and economic terrains of transnational migration.

items.title: Digital Technology Utilization at Lataban National High School: Digitization Model
items.abstract: This study assessed the digital technology utilization of junior high school students at Lataban National High School, Liloan, Cebu, during School Year 2025–2026 as the basis for developing a Digitization Model. Anchored in constructivist, connectivist, academic learning, and literacy-development perspectives, the study employed a descriptive-correlational research design involving 75 Grade 9 and Grade 10 students selected through total enumeration. Data were gathered using an adapted questionnaire and analyzed through frequencies, percentages, weighted means, standard deviations, and Pearson product-moment correlation. Findings revealed that respondents demonstrated very high technological skills (M = 4.24) and high levels of personal security, critical thinking, device security, informational, and communication skills. Digital tool utilization was high in online collaboration (M = 4.12), artificial intelligence in education (M = 3.96), electronic boards for learning (M = 3.42), and excessive technology use (M = 3.82). Internet resources (M = 3.50) and open-source AI tools (M = 3.42) showed high availability, while AI subscriptions (M = 3.19) and laptops (M = 3.29) demonstrated moderate availability. A significant positive relationship was established between digital technology utilization skills and digital tool utilization (r = 0.62, p < 0.05), resulting in the rejection of the null hypothesis. The study recommended strengthening digital competencies, improving technological resources, promoting responsible AI utilization, and progressively implementing the proposed Digitization Model. The research supports Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 4 on Quality Education, SDG 9 on Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure, and SDG 10 on Reduced Inequalities. Its sustainability implications involve promoting equitable digital learning opportunities, responsible technology utilization, and evidence-based institutional improvements toward inclusive and sustainable educational digitalization.

items.title: Digital Transformation and Organizational Performance: The Role of Technology-Driven Management Practices
items.abstract: Digital transformation has emerged as a strategic imperative for organizations seeking to improve operational efficiency, managerial effectiveness, innovation capabilities, and sustainable competitive advantage. The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI), big data analytics, cloud computing, the Internet of Things (IoT), enterprise resource planning (ERP), and digital communication technologies has fundamentally changed organizational structures, business processes, and managerial decision-making practices. In an increasingly competitive and technologically interconnected business environment, organizations are required to integrate digital technologies with strategic management practices to enhance productivity, organizational agility, employee performance, and overall business effectiveness. This research article examines the relationship between digital transformation and organizational performance, with particular emphasis on the mediating role of technology-driven management practices. The study adopts a systematic literature review-oriented conceptual approach, drawing upon established theoretical frameworks, including the Resource-Based View, Dynamic Capabilities Theory, Technology–Organization–Environment Framework, and Sociotechnical Systems Theory. It explores how digital leadership, data-driven decision-making, process automation, digital human resource management, technology-enabled financial management, and organizational innovation contribute to improved business performance. The conceptual analysis indicates that digital transformation can contribute to organizational performance when technological investments are supported by effective leadership, employee digital competencies, organizational adaptability, and appropriate governance mechanisms. However, cybersecurity risks, resistance to organizational change, inadequate digital infrastructure, financial constraints, and technological skill gaps may restrict the realization of these benefits. The article proposes an integrated conceptual framework explaining the relationship between digital transformation, technology-driven management practices, organizational capabilities, and organizational performance. It concludes that successful digital transformation requires a comprehensive managerial approach that integrates technological innovation with human capital development, strategic alignment, ethical governance, and continuous organizational learning.

items.title: Digital transformation support through EDIH services: a case study of DAP and FCO implementation in Croatia
items.abstract: Digital transformation support services help organisations translate digitalisation needs into structured investment and implementation plans. This study examines two advisory instruments delivered within the EDIH Adria project in Croatia: the Digitalisation Action Plan (DAP) and the Funding Capabilities and Opportunities (FCO) Assessment. It analyses documentation for 30 service users, comprising 13 small- and medium-sized enterprises and 17 public institutions, collected during 2024–2025. A descriptive and analytical approach examined technological domains, implementation periods, estimated investment costs, service duration and planned organisational impacts. The results show that 25 users received DAP services and 24 received FCO assessments, with 19 receiving both. Artificial intelligence and Decision support was the dominant technological domain, accounting for 12 DAP projects, followed by Internet of Things with 4 projects. Most projects had implementation periods of 6–12 months, while the most common investment categories were €50,000–€100,000 and above €100,000, with 8 projects in each category. The findings indicate that EDIH advisory services help structure diverse digital transformation initiatives. For practitioners, the results highlight the value of combining strategic planning with financial readiness assessment. For policymakers, they provide evidence on technology demand, investment requirements and organisational needs to inform regional and national digitalisation support programmes.

items.title: Digitalization and AI in Cementing
items.abstract: This chapter discusses how contemporary cementing operations are becoming digitalized and artificial intelligence (AI) that is just about to transform how one plans, performs, and optimizes their work, and how data-driven technologies are transforming cementing operations. Internet of Things (IoT) systems can help to monitor in real time the critical parameters (slurry density, flow rate, pressure, temperature, and equipment health) and prevent intermittency problems. These interrelated networked sensors are backed by trusted communication networks and cloud computing to enable a complete digital workflow that can be more aware of processes and manage them. Predictive and prescriptive cementing is introduced through the application of artificial intelligence and the application of machine learning. Slurry performance prediction, formulation optimization, and additive selection, operational risk estimation, and equipment fault prediction are forecasted using data-driven models through condition-driven maintenance. The chapter also discusses the application of digital twin technology that integrates real-time data and physics-based simulation to develop dynamic virtual models of cementing operations. These systems facilitate scenario analysis prior to the job, real-time optimization, anomaly detection, and post-job performance. The ability to collaborate remotely and make decisions all at once through cloud-based data management, standardized data architecture, and real-time dashboards allows subject matter experts to oversee a variety of operations at once. The advances into automation and remote operation centers are also mentioned, covering closed-loop control of mixing, pumping, and density control. The chapter incorporates a comprehensive approach to smart cementing, as it is 178 founded on integrating IoT and AI, digital twins, and automation in improving the safety and efficiency of the processes, precision of cement positioning, and compliance. This revolution in information symbolizes the shift in the responsive functions towards predictive, autonomous, and information-based well-building methods.

items.title: Disclosing the Machine in Human-AI Communication: A Scoping Review of Transparency Strategies, Trust, Authenticity, and Contextual Boundaries
items.abstract: This registration documents a scoping review examining how artificial intelligence (AI) disclosure and transparency are conceptualized, operationalized, and evaluated across human-AI communication contexts. The review focuses on four analytically distinct transparency objects: source disclosure, identity disclosure, authorship disclosure, and algorithmic transparency. The review maps disclosure strategies, communication and psychological mechanisms, contextual boundary conditions, user outcomes, methodological characteristics, and evidence gaps. Particular attention is given to trust, credibility, authenticity, social presence, perceived transparency, psychological reactance, mind perception, legitimacy, engagement, acceptance, and related behavioral outcomes. The review follows a Population-Concept-Context (PCC) eligibility framework and draws on literature identified through Scopus and Web of Science Core Collection. Searches were conducted on 28 October 2026 using terms related to artificial intelligence, human-AI communication, and AI disclosure or transparency. After database filtering and deduplication, 146 unique records were screened and 20 sources were included in the final evidence map, comprising 17 primary empirical studies, two secondary syntheses, and one conceptual or perspective article. Findings are synthesized descriptively and thematically and are further organized through a Disclosure-Context-Mechanism-Outcome (DCMO) framework. The framework conceptualizes AI disclosure as a communication process in which disclosure characteristics acquire meaning within specific contexts, activate interpretive mechanisms, and produce different evaluative or behavioral outcomes. This OSF registration is retrospective. The literature search, screening, data charting, methodological appraisal, evidence synthesis, and initial manuscript preparation had already been completed before registration. The record is therefore intended to provide a transparent and time-stamped account of the review methods and should not be interpreted as a prospective preregistration.

items.title: Do large language models hallucinate more in Uzbek? A cross-lingual measurement of factual reliability and its implications for non-English higher education
items.abstract: Introduction Students in non-English higher education are increasingly using large language models (LLMs) as informal study aids; however, the factual reliability of these systems in lower-resource languages - and its consequences for learning - remain largely unmeasured. Methods We report a controlled, fully reproducible evaluation of factual hallucination in eight open-weight LLMs answering 100 verifiable factual questions in English, Russian, and Uzbek. Uzbek, an agglutinative and comparatively low-resource Turkic language, is the primary language of instruction at our institution. Responses were scored with a deterministic answer-key procedure. Results The factual error rate increased monotonically with the resource level of the query language: 3.5% in English, 10.9% in Russian, and 15.9% in Uzbek (pooled over models; chi-square = 68.5, df = 2, p < 10 -14 ). The gap was present in nearly every model, but its size varied widely: a 12B general-purpose model answered reliably across all three languages, whereas the smaller 1-4B models had an error rate of 24%-27% in Uzbek. Language-adapted models - open checkpoints continued-pretrained or fine-tuned on Uzbek - closed the gap almost entirely, reaching an error rate of 2%-8% in Uzbek, comparable to their reliability in English. Discussion A student querying an off-the-shelf model in Uzbek is several times more likely to receive an incorrect fact than an English-speaking peer, which is both an equity concern and a hazard for academic integrity when unverified output enters student work. The risk, however, is not intrinsic to the language: it can be substantially reduced by preferring language-adapted models and by auditing per-language reliability before classroom deployment. All questions, code, and model outputs are released to support replication.

items.title: Does Working in Proximity to Drones Affect Workers’ Postural Balance? A Mixed-Reality Study
items.abstract: Drones are increasingly used on construction sites. However, close-proximity drone operations may produce visual and auditory disturbances that compromise workers’ postural balance and increase the risk of falls, trips, and slips, especially in hazardous work environments such as sloped roofs. Despite these concerns, empirical evidence on this issue remains limited. To address this gap, this study conducted a mixed-reality roofing experiment, in which a virtual drone approached and hovered at a distance of 0.45 m. Thirty-one participants were required to install shingles under both no-drone and near-drone conditions. Wearable insole sensors collected plantar pressure and center-of-pressure data. Five balance-related metrics were calculated and compared between conditions. Results showed that near-drone presence increased mean COP velocity for both feet and right-foot M/L COP displacement. These findings provide preliminary evidence that close-proximity drone operations may increase workers’ postural control demands, highlighting the need for future research on human-centered deployment strategies in construction.

items.title: DolphinRouting: Cluster-Level Binary Routing for Disaggregated LLM Inference Serving
items.abstract: Prefill-decode (PD) disaggregation isolates the two phases of large language model serving, but request-level path selection must account for prefill work, cache reuse, and decode demand. We present DolphinRouting, which learns this choice from end-to-end SLO feedback under a given P/D resource allocation. Requests are clustered by raw prompt length, cache-adjusted input lengths on both worker pools, and output-length information. Offline policy search learns one binary action per cluster. Online feature extraction, cluster assignment, and table lookup select local or remote prefill. We evaluate DolphinRouting on a real PD-disaggregated cluster using three public benchmarks, a mixed workload, and real data. Across the mixed workload and real data, DolphinRouting with $k$-means reduces P90 TTFT by 5.7--7.9\% and P90 TPOT by 2.6--10.1\% relative to Dynamo.

items.title: Domestic Assistive Robots’ Approach in Daily Living Activities for Older Adults
items.abstract: Domestic assistive robots can support older adults with daily tasks such as medication delivery, but these interactions require robots to approach users within personal home spaces. Although, human-robot proxemics research shows that robot distance, speed, and movement direction affect user comfort, limited work has examined how older adults interpret these behaviors during domestic assistive handoff tasks. This study explored how six older adults perceived mobile robot manipulator notification style during a simulated medication delivery task in a home-like environment. Four scenarios varied by approach direction and verbal notification strategy, with attention to comfort, trust, and acceptance. Participants generally preferred an arm’s length interaction distance and described it as the most comfortable zone for medication handoff. Trust increased after repeated interaction across the scenarios. Findings suggest that domestic assistive robots should use predictable notification cues, maintain comfortable handoff distances, and allow adjustable speed and approach behaviors to support comfort, acceptance, and trust.

items.title: Dual-layer edge intelligence for secure real-time medical IoT: a Zero-Trust sequential framework integrating soft-voting intrusion detection and Histogram Gradient Boosting
items.abstract: Introduction The Internet of Medical Things (MIoT) enables continuous transmission of patient vital signs for real-time monitoring and clinical decision making in intensive care units. A lot of different and interdependent devices are used in these medical settings in order to ensure time and reliability for healthcare services. But with 24/7 connectivity comes the danger of cyberattacks, unauthorized access and tampered medical information. Cloud-based processing also causes delays in communication and reliance on network availability and could impact the timely delivery of critical clinical alerts. The current studies are mostly related to patient monitoring, or network intrusion detection, and only a few merge both these functions within a single edge computing setup. Methods This article proposes a Dual-Layer Edge Intelligence Framework for secure real-time Medical IoT. The framework executes two Artificial Intelligence modules sequentially on a ward-level edge node. A Security AI Module, built on a soft-voting ensemble, screens every network flow first and acts as a Zero-Trust gate. Only traffic that it clears as benign is passed to the Healthcare AI Module, built on Histogram Gradient Boosting, which screens the patient's physiological state for anomaly-based indicators of critical deterioration. This sequential design makes sure that none of the clinical decisions are taken based on unverified information, while at the same time making sure there is safe interaction between network management and healthcare analytics. The framework was tested with two benchmark datasets, which are CICIDS-2017 and MIMIC-IV. Results : The Security AI Module has an accuracy of 99.4% with a false positive rate of less than 2% and the Healthcare AI Module has a cross-validated accuracy of 98.97% and ROC-AUC of 0.995 with complete recall on all the validation folds. The complete sequential pipeline achieved an end-to-end latency of approximately 28.8 ms, making it suitable for real-time intensive care monitoring. Discussion A permissioned Hyperledger Fabric ledger with IPFS off-chain storage is presented as a conceptual future governance layer; it is not implemented or evaluated in this study. The findings show that adopting Zero-Trust security and clinical intelligence in one edge framework offers a viable paradigm for secure, low-latency, and trustworthy Medical IoT systems.

items.title: Dynamic analysis and spatiotemporal evolution of multi-stage knowledge dissemination under AI-enabled dual-channel “Interpersonal–Human-Machine” interaction
items.abstract: With the deep integration of digitalization and artificial intelligence technologies into enterprise knowledge management, AI-assisted learning is reshaping the channels through which knowledge is acquired within organizations. Meanwhile, knowledge dissemination is evolving from traditional interpersonal interaction toward human-machine collaborative interaction. In light of this transformation, this study develops a multi-stage 2 SEIR - CA dynamic model of knowledge dissemination under an AI-enabled mechanism that incorporates dual-channel “interpersonal–human-machine” interaction. Specifically, employees are classified into five states: employees who have not yet mastered the knowledge, employees with limited knowledge mastery, employees with strong knowledge mastery, knowledge-disseminating employees, and knowledge-exited employees. On this basis, the next-generation matrix method is employed to calculate the basic reproduction number of the system and to analyze the existence and stability of equilibrium points. An optimal control model is then established to derive strategies for promoting knowledge dissemination, and a cellular automaton model is introduced to characterize its spatiotemporal evolution. The results show that the system exhibits a pronounced threshold effect: when key dissemination parameters exceed their critical levels, knowledge can continue to diffuse within the organization; otherwise, it will gradually decay. Second, the AI-enabled mechanism enhances knowledge transformation efficiency and contact intensity, thereby significantly promoting the transition of employees with strong knowledge mastery to knowledge-disseminating employees. Third, the optimal control strategy proposed in this study can optimize transformation pathways across different stages under resource constraints, thereby improving overall dissemination efficiency and maintaining the structural stability of the dissemination system. Fourth, the spatiotemporal simulations demonstrate that, under optimal regulation, knowledge dissemination can form a stable diffusion pattern with high coverage. Under the assumptions and parameter settings of the proposed model, the findings provide theoretical insights into the dynamic mechanisms underlying AI-enabled knowledge dissemination and offer model-based implications for knowledge management practices in organizations.

items.title: Dynamic Optimization of Personalized English Learning Ability Enhancement Methods Driven by Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract: Intelligent and adaptive English language learning utilizes artificial intelligence to personalize the learning experience. Adapting English learning content in real-time, depending on individual student behavior and progress, is not possible with existing systems due to a lack of dynamic optimization. This proposed method is used to develop a dynamic, reinforcement learning-driven framework that adapts to each learner’s cognitive and emotional states, thereby enhancing individualized English language acquisition. This method uses Meta-Cognitive Reinforcement Learning (MCRL) to describe each learner as an intelligent agent with a dynamic state vector of proficiency, attentiveness, and tiredness. Based on reinforcement signals from learner performance and motivation, a meta-policy controller chooses optimal learning strategies and tasks. The results reveal that MCRL outperforms baseline systems in vocabulary, grammar, comprehension, learner engagement, and retention. Real-time adaptability is demonstrated by a 22% increase in learning efficiency and a reduction in task repetition. Results show that MCRL-based learners improved their average competency scores by 18% over four weeks while maintaining better engagement. Autonomously optimizing the learning path reduced cognitive fatigue and increased motivation. Ultimately, reinforcement learning enhances learning outcomes and the learner experience in individualized language instruction.

items.title: Early Prediction of Cross-Service Implementation Scope: Evidence and Limits from Multiple Microservice Projects
items.abstract: Microservice architectures aim to localize change, yet feature requests may require implementation across service boundaries. We investigate how well such downstream scope can be anticipated before implementation begins. Using issue--pull-request--commit traceability and implementation evidence corrected through targeted human adjudication, we reconstruct 866 repository-traceable feature requests from 13 open-source microservice projects and map their implementations to validated service boundaries. Cross-service changes occur in 101 requests (11.7%) and exhibit broader implementation footprints, particularly higher code churn, but no clear difference in lead time. Pre-implementation evidence provides limited cross-project predictive signal: the strongest leave-one-system-out model reaches a project-macro Macro-F1 of 0.484, but its advantage over the majority baseline is not significant after Holm correction and is sensitive to small evaluation folds. A local LLM offers no reliable improvement over classical models. Downstream workload is substantially harder to estimate, as learned models do not consistently outperform training-fold median baselines. A simple service-mention heuristic also performs comparably to learned scope triage. These findings show that early feature-request evidence is more useful for lightweight cross-service scope triage than for automated scope determination or precise workload estimation.

items.title: ECHO: A Longitudinal Study of Contextual Consistency and Alignment Limits in Large Language Models
items.abstract: ECHO (Evaluation of Contextual Consistency and Alignment Limits in Large Language Models) is a longitudinal research project investigating contextual retention, narrative coherence, corrective learning, and alignment limitations in Large Language Models (LLMs). The study is based on approximately 900 hours of human-AI interaction conducted over 90 consecutive days under real-world usage conditions. Unlike traditional benchmark evaluations focused on isolated tasks, ECHO analyzes long-term conversational behavior, contextual fidelity, adaptation to corrective feedback, and degradation patterns in extended interactions. The project also introduces the Contextual Fidelity Index (CFI), a proposed framework for evaluating contextual consistency in conversational AI systems. items.title: EdFitter: a hybrid course recommendation system using large language models
items.abstract: Educational institutions face increasing pressure to adapt their curricula to the rapidly evolving demands of the job market, and recommender systems can be important tools to guide students in selecting courses that align with their career goals. We present EdFitter, a hybrid course recommendation system that combines pretrained text embeddings for retrieval with large language models (LLMs) used offline for semantic skill extraction. The system is designed for a cold-start setting in which free-text job queries must be matched to a university’s institutional course catalog. Instead of relying on direct generative recommendations, EdFitter ranks stored course descriptions by cosine similarity and augments the output with extracted skills and matching vacancy examples. We evaluate the system in a pilot institutional deployment at Higher School of Economics (HSE) using a multi-level study with student respondents, controlled assessors, and interviews with program directors. The results indicate that users perceive the recommendations as sufficiently relevant and potentially useful to justify further development. Overall, the study suggests that EdFitter is a valuable tool for supporting course exploration and curriculum-to-labor-market alignment; we also highlight important limitations and directions for future work.

items.title: Effect of an Occupational Health and Safety Educational Intervention on Knowledge, Practices, Musculoskeletal Disorders, and Injuries Among Oilseed Processing Workers
items.abstract: Occupational hazards, injuries, work-related illnesses, and fatalities remain core public health challenges in industrial settings. Workers in oilseed processing factories are exposed to multiple occupational risks; however, evidence regarding the effectiveness of occupational health and safety educational interventions in these settings remains limited and not explored and examined. The main objective of this study is to evaluate the effect of educational program on workers occupational health and safety (OHS) knowledge, attitudes, practices, and the prevalence of occupational injuries in oilseed processing (OSP) factories. A quasi-experimental controlled pretest–posttest intervention study design will be conducted among 466 factory workers selected through simple random sampling and equally allocated to intervention and control groups. Around 466 workers recruited from 10 randomly selected OSP factories in Eastern Ethiopia. The factories will be purposively allocated into intervention (n = 5) and control (n = 5) groups based on geographical location, with 233 workers randomly selected from each group (1:1 allocation). Eligible participants will be factory workers aged ≥18 years with at least one year of employment. OHS Educational intervention program will be implemented for 3 months. The intervention consisted of a three-month OHS educational program incorporating health education sessions, on-the-job training, and informational leaflets. Data will be collected at baseline and post-intervention. Data will be entered using Epi-Data and analyzed in STATA version 16.1. Between-group differences will be assessed using chi-square, independent t-, and Mann-Whitney tests. Multivariable logistic regression and generalized estimating equations (GEE) will be applied to estimate intervention effects using a difference-in-differences approach. Statistical significance will be set at p < 0.05. Regarding ethics and dissemination, Ethical approval was obtained from the Jimma University Institute of Health Institutional Review Board (Ref: JUIH/IRPB/217/25). Findings will be disseminated through collaboration with factory management, health professionals, government agencies, community stakeholders, and non-governmental organizations to facilitate the implementation and scale-up of effective workplace OHS interventions. This study will generate robust evidence on the effectiveness of an OHS educational program in enhancing workers OHS knowledge, attitudes, and practices while reducing or not occupational injuries and work-related Musculo-skeletal disorders (WMSDs) among OSP factories workers in Ethiopia. The study is expected to generate context-specific evidence that can inform workplace OHS policies and guide the development of feasible, evidence-based interventions for industrial workers in Ethiopia. At the time of reporting, the intervention is started but not completed, and post-intervention data collection is also not completed.

items.title: Efficient biological design via genomic in-context learning
items.abstract: In-context learning (ICL), the ability to perform new tasks from a few examples supplied in a prompt, is a defining emergent capability of large language models. Here, we show that ICL emerges in the genome language model Evo 2 and enables biological design. With as few as four examples in the prompt and no additional training, Evo 2 generates realistic metal-binding proteins, de novo antibodies, protein-RNA systems, and entire bacteriophage genomes. For ΦX174-like bacteriophage design, ICL surpasses previously fine-tuned models on computational measures of design quality and diversity. Beyond ΦX174, conditioning the model with different phage prompts enables us to efficiently design MS2 and M13 genomes in silico without fine-tuning. Iteratively updating the prompt with newly generated phage genomes, which we refer to as genomic chain-of-thought, further improves the diversity of designs while maintaining quality metrics. Paired with an inference engine that accelerates generation up to 35-fold and extends practicable context to a megabase, these results establish ICL as a versatile and efficient paradigm for biological sequence design.

items.title: Electric Vehicle Smart Charging Systems
items.abstract: The rapid growth of Electric Vehicles is transforming modern transportation while creating major challenges for power grid stability, including peak load demand, energy imbalance, and renewable energy integration. To address these issues, smart EV charging systems have emerged as intelligent solutions capable of optimizing charging operations according to grid conditions, electricity pricing, and user needs. This chapter presents a comprehensive review of Artificial Intelligence and optimization techniques applied to EV smart charging systems. It analyzes machine learning, deep learning, deterministic, stochastic, and heuristic optimization methods, as well as hybrid AI–optimization frameworks. The study highlights their benefits in improving charging efficiency, reducing operational costs, enhancing load balancing, and supporting grid stability. Furthermore, current limitations such as scalability, computational complexity, and data dependency are discussed, alongside research gaps related to renewable energy integration, decentralized control, and real-time adaptive management.

items.title: Elevated ZnO Concentrations as a Trade-Off Strategy to Decrease Spindle Speeds in Face Milling
items.abstract: Higher productivity, lower cost, environmental requirement and occupational health have become serious challenges for manufacturing industries nowadays. In this study, a mixture comprising canola oil, emulsifier and ZnO nanoparticles was applied as the cutting oil for face milling of stainless steel SS316L. Previous studies have demonstrated decreasing surface roughness with increasing spindle speed. Numerous previous studies have also revealed decreasing surface roughness with increasing ZnO concentrations. However, a relationship between elevated ZnO concentrations and reduced spindle speeds has barely been addressed. Building on this circumstance, a novel machining strategy was proposed in this study by employing elevated ZnO concentrations as a trade-off strategy to reduce the spindle speeds. The spindle speeds in this study were 1500, 1800 and 2100 rpm. The experiment demonstrated that elevating ZnO concentrations from 1.0 to 4.0 wt% could be used to decrease the spindle speeds from 2100 to 1800 rpm while maintaining acceptable surface roughness. Although future studies are warranted, reducing spindle speed is beneficial for manufacturing industries as it may contribute to lower electrical energy consumption. Furthermore, the proposed trade-off strategy can also be implemented for manufacturing industries located in regions with limited electrical grid capacity, for example, due to restricted capacity of electrical transformers.

items.title: Emerging Computational Advances in Simulating PCSK9 Variant Dynamics for Therapeutic Design Against Hypercholesterolemia
items.abstract: Proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) is a premier model for precision medicine, having moved from genetic discovery to approved therapeutics within two decades. Yet despite the clinical success of monoclonal antibodies, small interfering RNA and the newly approved oral macrocyclic-peptide inhibitor class, targeting PCSK9 remains a demanding biophysical challenge. Clinical translation has concentrated almost entirely on the rigid, well-resolved subtilisin-like catalytic domain that interfaces with the low-density lipoprotein receptor (LDLR). By contrast, the C-terminal cysteine- and histidine-rich domain (CHRD), which governs allosteric regulation, protein trafficking and post-translational modification, is highly disordered and largely elusive in experimental structures, leaving a critical regulatory network therapeutically unexploited. This review examines how advanced computational biology is bridging that structural gap, organizing the computational landscape of PCSK9 around the biophysical mechanisms of gain- and loss-of-function variants. We detail how explicit-solvent molecular dynamics, free-energy calculations and cryptic-pocket detection expose the functional plasticity and allosteric networks that static crystallography cannot capture, and we evaluate the convergence of these physics-based approaches with artificial intelligence, including deep-learning structure prediction and generative design of de novo nanobody and peptide binders. Therapeutic development and the structural literature currently point in diverging directions: drug discovery remains focused on the crowded LDLR-binding interface, whereas computational methods are beginning to identify candidate sites beyond it. We argue that the next advance in PCSK9 therapeutics will come from integrating generative artificial intelligence with rigorous enhanced sampling in a unified pipeline, deliberately shifting focus toward the disordered regulatory domains that have evaded classical screening.

items.title: Emerging sociotechnical imaginaries of Edtech and AI in education policy discourse in Nigeria
items.abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the dominant actor imaginaries of Edtech and Artificial Intelligence in education (AIED) embedded in Nigerian policy discourse under the Tinubu administration, and the argumentation strategies used to legitimise them. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on the Discourse-Historical Approach (DHA), this study combines a socio-historical analysis with an analysis of a corpus of public texts emerging from the most salient events related to this policy discourse in Nigeria since 2023. Findings Education policy discourse in Nigeria is increasingly driven by a sociotechnical imaginary that positions Edtech and AI as a solution to the persistent problem of education access and equality, and as a catalyst for economic growth. This discourse frames local actors as lacking capacity, and collaboration with transnational corporate and philanthropic actors as necessary to provide the technical, financial, and institutional capacity. It also rests on a demographic argument that constructs the country’s large youth population as a demographic risk/opportunity, whose value lies in its capacity to be mobilised as a workforce for the emerging global technologies market. Through these narratives, traditional actors, who have historically played important roles in education governance, are excluded from the policy networks shaping dominant education discourses. Originality/value This study contributes theoretically to the growing body of research on developing new methodologies to describe new actors present in education policy and empirically supports understanding the flow of sociotechnical imaginaries through networked governance within an under-researched postcolonial context.

items.title: Emotional and behavioral asymmetries in user responses to virtual versus human influencers
items.abstract: As AI virtual influencers (AIVIs) proliferate, understanding human-AI emotional engagement is vital for advancing affective computing. To examine whether AIVIs evoke comparable affective responses to human influencers (HIs), we analyzed 156,918 Instagram comments that received 12+ million likes, integratinglarge language model (LLM)-derived knowledge graphs, emotion analysis, and machine learning. HI-directed discourse shows more differentiated emotional expression and a pattern consistent with more cohesive semantic networks than AIVI-directed discourse. AIVI-directed comments are less likely to express positive affect (24.8% vs. 41.5%) and also less likely to express negative affect (5.8% vs. 9.3%), indicating reduced affective expression of either valence rather than heightened negativity. This group-level tendency is not uniform: affective engagement varies substantially across AIVIs, and that variation is more closely associated with positive than with negative expression. Our Multi-Signal Embedding Network (MSEN), incorporating behavioral metrics and OpenAI semantic embeddings, classified influencer types from behavioral, affective and semantic features (F1 = 0.89), outperforming baselines including a state-of-the-art zero-shot LLM. These findings identify a boundary condition for the Computers Are Social Actors (CASA) paradigm: human-like appearance can elicit social responses without producing affective and semantic response patterns as rich as those elicited by HIs.

items.title: EMPLOYEE WELL-BEING PROGRAMS AND MEASURABLE RETURNS ON INVESTIMENT IN PRIVATE INSTITUTIONS
items.abstract: Employee well-being has is no longer viewed only as an employee-support activity to becoming an important component of strategic human resource management. Apparently many organizations are increasingly investing in employee assistance programmes, mental-health support, flexible work, health promotion, financial well-being, manager training, occupational health, and other interventions. The focus managerial question, however, is whether these programmes produce measurable equitable financial returns. So this article examines that question critically by distinguishing return on investment (ROI) from broader organizational value, reviewing evidence on absenteeism, presenteeism, turnover, productivity, engagement, health costs and organizational performance, and identifying the methodological difficulties involved in attributing business outcomes to well-being interventions. The evidences lament that well-designed programs can generate measurable benefits, but a positive financial ROI should not be assumed. Results vary subsequently according to intervention type, implementation quality, work force characteristics, and time horizon and evaluation design. Systematic reviews provide a blended picture in a way that some workplace prevention interventions report positive economic outcomes, while higher-quality studies of some wellness programs have found little or zero short-term financial ROI. This means that Human Resource professionals should avoid treating well-being as either an automatic cost or a source of savings. Instead, organizations should identify the specific workforce problem, select evidence-informed interventions, establish baseline measures, use comparison groups where possible, calculate total program costs, and evaluate outcomes over an appropriate period of time. The article concludes with an HR evaluation framework that integrates financial ROI with employee, operational and strategic measures. It also discusses different implications for organizations in developing economies, including Uganda, where resource constraints make evidence-based prioritization particularly important.
